intro: If you're planning a trip to the eastern side of Chanthaburi — splashing around at Phlio Waterfall, strolling Nong Bua Walking Street, or just looking for a quiet place to tuck yourself away for a few hundred baht a night — Chimphli Hotel is a small garden hotel in Khlung District that a lot of people overlook because it isn't in the town centre · It's a 20-room stay on Thetsaban Sai 9 Road in Khlung subdistrict, with a leafy garden, a terrace to relax on, and free parking right at your door, which is super convenient if you're driving · It's about 15 min drive from Namtok Phlio National Park · Rooms start at about THB 700/night, with a real review score of 8.4 out of 10 on Trip.com, and it has even picked up a Travelers' Choice award from Tripadvisor — small, but it wins over the people who actually stay there.

body.html: Chimphli Hotel overview — who it's for — Let me be straight with you first: Chimphli Hotel isn't a luxury hotel and isn't trying to be · It's a 20-room small garden hotel in Khlung District, a little district in the east of Chanthaburi province bordering Trat · What it's selling is quiet, cleanliness, and a price that's very easy on the wallet for what you get · The people it suits best are travellers who are driving themselves and want a base for a trip out to Phlio Waterfall, the beaches at Laem Sing, or passing in and out of the Trat border · After that come couples or small families who want a quiet, fuss-free place — they don't need loads of facilities, just a clean room, cold air-con, and safe parking · The people it may not suit are those who mainly want to explore central Chanthaburi and walk the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, because it's a fair way out of town, a 20–30 min drive into the city · Real reviews sum the place up the same way: "good value, clean, easy parking right at your door," which, for a 2-star hotel in a small district, carries real weight · The hotel is still open and operating normally and takes bookings across several platforms — Trip.com, Agoda, Klook, and Hotels.com — so there's no need to worry about it being an abandoned or closed-down stay.

Location and getting there — Chimphli Hotel sits at 2/1 Thetsaban Sai 9 Road, Khlung subdistrict, Khlung District, a quiet residential area within Khlung town itself · The thing to understand is that Khlung District is about 25–30 km east of Chanthaburi town along Sukhumvit Road (Highway 3) · The upside of this location is that it's very close to Namtok Phlio National Park — about a 15-minute drive to the waterfall entrance, the most popular waterfall in Chanthaburi, with clear pools, schools of soro brook carp, and an old chedi from the reign of King Rama V · It's also not far from Nong Bua Walking Street and the coast at Laem Sing, making it an easy base for exploring the eastern side · On getting around, I'll be honest: this place suits people with their own car the most, because public transport in Khlung District is limited — just the Chanthaburi–Khlung songthaew that runs on a schedule · One review says plainly that "the entrance is fairly far out and a little hard to find," so if it's your first visit, I'd recommend turning on GPS navigation and calling the hotel ahead to ask for directions · For those flying in, the nearest airport is Trat Airport, about 23 km away, while anyone coming from Bangkok is looking at a long drive of about 3.5–4 hr along Sukhumvit Road.

"Great value for the price, clean room, and you can park right at your door — so convenient. Perfect for anyone driving out to Phlio Waterfall. The entrance is just a little hard to find, so keep your map navigation on and it'll be easier."

Room types and decor — Being a small hotel, there are around 20 rooms in total, split into just a few main types · The entry-level room is the Superior Double Room with one queen bed, stepping up to the Deluxe Double Room with a king bed for people who want more space and a bigger bed · Every room is air-conditioned, with a flat-screen TV, a private bathroom with shower, and free drinking water · The decor is simple and clean — nothing fancy, but the focus is on being clean and genuinely usable, which is what reviews mention most often — plenty of people praise how clean the rooms and bathrooms are, with no musty smell or grime issues, which matters a lot at this price · A detail many guests love is that nearly all the rooms are single-storey units lined up in the garden, so you can park right at your door and carry your bags straight in and out without dragging them through a lobby or up a lift · One thing guests have mentioned is that the blankets are fairly thin, so if you feel the cold easily or run the air-con very cold, you may want to ask the hotel for an extra blanket or bring a light cover of your own · Overall the rooms here deliver on "comfortable to sleep in, clean, good value" rather than being rooms you come to for luxury, which is exactly what the price told you from the start.

Facilities and the garden atmosphere — Chimphli Hotel has no swimming pool, gym, or spa, because it's a small hotel in a small district, so you shouldn't expect big-resort facilities · But what it does have, and does well, is a garden and terrace — shady and green, perfect for sipping coffee in the morning or relaxing after a day out at the waterfall · The overall feel is very quiet, since it's in a residential area with none of the busy traffic noise you get in town · The basics for an overnight stay are all covered: free Wi-Fi throughout, free parking at your door, free drinking water, and daily housekeeping · There's a small in-house dining room for simple meals · The thing many guests especially like is the parking — you park right in front of your room, safe and convenient, a small detail that puts road-trippers at ease · If I had to compare, the place feels more like a garden guesthouse than a typical hotel — nothing flashy, but everything you need, and clean.

Food and places to eat nearby — On food, you need to understand the location first · Chimphli Hotel is a small hotel and doesn't sell a buffet-breakfast package like the big hotels do · There's a small in-house dining room for simple meals and free drinking water, but the real strength is the restaurants around Khlung District · Khlung District and this side of Chanthaburi are known for fresh seafood and local food — there are seafood spots like Sornpochana about a 10 min drive away, and dessert cafés like Sugar Dish Homemade Cake about an 11-minute drive · If you like Chanthaburi local dishes, there's sen chan stir-fried with crab, kuaytiao mu liang, and seasonal fruit including durian, rambutan, and mangosteen (if you come during fruit season around April–June) · For a simple breakfast in Khlung town there are plenty of coffee shops and rice-soup/congee places to choose from · In short, this place suits people who like heading out to find food rather than eating in the hotel, which fits a road trip on the eastern side of Chanthaburi perfectly · I'd suggest stocking some water and snacks in the car, since at certain times the shops in a small district can close early.

Service — Since it's a small, family-run hotel, the reviews on service lean warm and friendly · Many guests say the owner and staff take good care of them, answer questions about routes and places to visit, and help you feel as relaxed as if you were staying at a relative's place rather than a hotel · With only 20 rooms, the care is thorough and not as hectic as a big, crowded hotel · The expectation to set correctly is that there's no chain-hotel service here — no concierge, no 24-hour room service, no tour desk · If you need something special, like a late check-in or an extra blanket, I'd recommend calling ahead, because staff may not be at the counter around the clock the way they are at a big hotel · Overall, for a stay at this level, the service is better than expected and is one of the things that adds to the sense of value for what you pay.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — Pulling together Trip.com and other booking platforms, the picture is fairly consistent, even though the number of reviews is still small because it's a little hotel · On the praise side: value for money is what gets mentioned most, the rooms and bathrooms are clean, parking at your door is convenient and safe, the atmosphere is quiet and good for resting, and the location is close to Phlio Waterfall for road-trippers · The overall score on Trip.com sits at 8.4 out of 10 in the "very good" range, and the hotel has also earned a Travelers' Choice award from Tripadvisor, which goes to stays that get consistently good reviews · On the watch-out side: what comes up is that the entrance is fairly far out and hard to find for first-timers without GPS, the blankets are fairly thin for people who feel the cold, and the fact that you really need your own car to make it convenient, since it's not somewhere you can walk to things · These gripes are all things you can manage with a bit of preparation rather than quality problems with the rooms or cleanliness, which is a good sign for a budget stay.

"Stayed here before heading to Phlio Waterfall in the morning — nice and quiet, slept well, clean bathroom · The blanket was a bit thin so I asked the hotel for an extra one and they brought it right over. For this price it's really pretty good."

Price comparison and value — Room rates at Chimphli Hotel start at about THB 700/night for the Superior Double, rising to around THB 800–1,000 for the Deluxe Double or over long weekends and fruit season · At this price level, it's great value for people who just want a clean place to sleep and safe parking near Phlio Waterfall · Compared with a hotel in Chanthaburi town like Kasemsarn Hotel, which starts around THB 900 but sits in the centre where you can walk and explore the Chanthaboon Riverside · The difference is that Chimphli focuses on the eastern location near the waterfall and on quiet, while town hotels focus on the convenience of walking around the old quarter · If your trip centres on Phlio Waterfall, the beaches at Laem Sing, or passing through to Trat, staying in Khlung genuinely saves both driving time and fuel · But if you're set on exploring central Chanthaburi, paying a little more to stay in town may be the better deal · The bottom line is that the value here depends on which side of the province your itinerary sits — if it matches Khlung, this is one of the best-value options in the area.

What to know before you book — A few things will make your stay smoother · One, this place suits people with a car the most — if you don't have your own car, check the Chanthaburi–Khlung songthaew schedule or arrange a hired ride ahead of time · Two, turn on GPS navigation and save the coordinates, because reviews say the entrance is a little hard to find for first-timers · Three, if you feel the cold easily or run the air-con very cold, plan to ask for an extra blanket at check-in, as the standard blanket is fairly thin · Four, if you're coming during fruit season (April–June), which is Chanthaburi's high season, book ahead because there are only 20 rooms and they fill up fast · Five, call the hotel ahead if you'll check in late, since it's a small hotel that may not have staff at the counter 24 hours · Six, keep some food and water in the car, as shops in a small district can close early at certain times.

The verdict — From everything real reviews say, Chimphli Hotel is the best fit for travellers driving the eastern side of Chanthaburi who want a clean place to sleep, quiet, and easy parking, at an easy price near Phlio Waterfall · It's not a hotel you come to for luxury — no pool, no spa, and it's out of town — but what it promises (clean, good value, friendly, parking at your door) it delivers in full and well enough to earn an 8.4 and a Travelers' Choice award · If you're planning to visit Phlio Waterfall, the beaches at Laem Sing, Nong Bua Walking Street, or passing through to Trat, this is a tidy, budget-friendly base · But if you're set on exploring central Chanthaburi and walking the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, or you want full resort facilities, consider a stay in town instead · Match it to the right kind of trip and Chimphli Hotel will be the little stay that makes your Chanthaburi trip smooth and better value than the price suggests.
